title: Zephyrine and the Orchard
premise: In the winter of 1917, Mirabel Oyelaran, a colonial-born nurse stationed at a coastal field hospital, keeps a private ledger of soldiers' names and last words — the ones the officers' dispatches leave out. When the season's bridge closure strands her in the orchard village of Zephyrine with a dying colonel's confession, she realizes the official history will erase everyone she has tended. Racing against the spring tide that will carry the victors' historians home, Mirabel must choose between loyalty to the army that gave her shelter and the truth owed to the dead. She smuggles the ledger aboard the historians' ship at dawn, trading her own anonymity for a record that will outlast them all.
about_author: Theo Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters from the First World War. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the field hospital at Zephyrine, Mirabel records names officers omit from dispatches, believing history happens elsewhere, to other people. A young soldier dies asking her to remember him properly. Emotional beat: quiet defiance disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Dispatches and Omissions
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She compares her ledger to the official reports Colonel Ashworth files and finds whole platoons vanished from the record. Her friend Sister Agnes warns her that curiosity is a luxury for people with papers. Emotional beat: first crack in her belief in invisibility.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Flood season closes the only road out of Zephyrine; supply convoys halt, orders stop arriving, and the hospital becomes an island. Mirabel feels relief she's ashamed of. Emotional beat: the strange freedom of being stranded.

chapters.title: An Orchard in Winter
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. With lulls between casualties, villagers draw her into orchard life — pruning, cider, shared bread. The Vasseau family treats her as a neighbor, not a subject of empire. Emotional beat: belonging arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Confession
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Dying Colonel Ashworth summons her and confesses he falsified casualty figures after a disastrous ordered advance, naming the men erased. He asks her to set it right before the historians' ship sails on the morning tide. Emotional beat: burden transferred, unwanted inheritance.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: Sister Agnes's POV. Agnes discovers the confession and urges silence: the army protects them, feeds them, shields them. Mirabel argues truth is also a debt. Emotional beat: friendship strained along the fault line of loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: The Historians Arrive Early
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Two official historians arrive ahead of schedule, billeted at the hospital, interviewing officers and sketching a clean narrative of the campaign. Mirabel recognizes one as a man whose name is in her ledger under 'deserted.' Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Reading the Enemy's Draft
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She glimpses the historians' draft chapter glorifying the advance Ashworth confessed to. Every omitted name confirmed as deliberate erasure. She begins copying her ledger by candlelight. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the race has begun.

chapters.title: Cider and Testimony
chapters.summary: Vasseau matriarch Odile's POV. Odile, who lost two sons in the advance, shares the family's own account with Mirabel over cider — dates, letters, a photograph. Emotional beat: grief offered freely, becoming evidence.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The historian Captain Reeve catches Mirabel watching him and, charmingly, probes her background — her colonial papers make her vulnerable. He hints that nurses who gossip lose their posts. Emotional beat: threat wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: Agnes Chooses
chapters.summary: Sister Agnes's POV. Torn, Agnes secretly burns nothing but hides Mirabel's original ledger inside a crate of bandages bound for the ship, without telling her why. Emotional beat: loyalty finding its own path to truth.

chapters.title: The Flood Rises
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The river floods the lower ward; patients and villagers work side by side through the night to move the wounded. In exhaustion, class and rank dissolve. Emotional beat: community forged in emergency.

chapters.title: Ashworth's Last Night
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The colonel dies at dawn, whispering corrections to his own confession. Mirabel records his death honestly — including the falsification — knowing it could damn or redeem him. Emotional beat: mercy and accuracy wrestling.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Captain Reeve's POV. Reeve, uneasy himself, interviews Mirabel formally and realizes she knows more than any nurse should. He offers her protection in exchange for the ledger. Emotional beat: temptation framed as rescue.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel refuses, invoking her duty to the dead. Reeve, shaken, reveals he lost a brother whose name appears nowhere in any report. Emotional beat: adversary revealed as fellow mourner.

chapters.title: The Plan at the Orchard Wall
chapters.summary: Mirabel, Agnes, and Odile's alternating POVs. The three women plan to get the ledger aboard the historians' ship before the morning tide: Agnes's bandage crate, Odile's cart, Mirabel's nerve. Emotional beat: conspiracy of the overlooked.

chapters.title: Complications at the Quay
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The crate is delayed at inspection; Reeve is ordered to search all outbound goods. Mirabel must distract him while Odile reroutes the ledger through fish barrels. Emotional beat: terror braided with absurdity.

chapters.title: Reeve's Decision
chapters.summary: Captain Reeve's POV. Alone with the discovered ledger, Reeve reads his brother's name among the counted dead. He seals the crate and marks it cleared. Emotional beat: a man choosing conscience over career.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The ship sails with the ledger aboard; Mirabel watches from the quay, unsure if it will matter, certain it was right. The bridge reopens behind her. Emotional beat: release after long-held breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Accusation
chapters.summary: Sister Agnes's POV. An inquiry arrives asking who leaked documents; suspicion falls on the hospital staff. Agnes claims sole responsibility, protecting Mirabel. Emotional beat: loyalty repaid at cost.

chapters.title: The Record Holds
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Months later, a printed correction reaches Zephyrine — the historians' revised account includes the omitted names, credited to 'an unnamed nurse of the Zephyrine ward.' Odile plants a tree for each son. Emotional beat: vindication, quiet and incomplete.

chapters.title: Zephyrine and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Spring opens the orchard; Mirabel, offered transfer home, chooses to stay and train local nurses, beginning a new ledger — this time of the living. Emotional beat: belonging chosen at last; inheritance accepted.
